Judgment

1. Vide this judgment, this court shall dispose of the present revision petition filed by the revisionists u/s 397/399 of Cr.P.C. assailing the order dated 19-05-2022 and charge framed dated 18-11-2022 passed by the court of Ms. Renu Chaudhary, Ld. MM, North-East Distt. KKD, Delhi by virtue of which, the Ld. Trial Court has framed charge against Avdhesh Kumar for the offence punishable u/s 498A/406 of IPC and discharged remaining respondents for the offences punishable u/s 498A/406 IPC.
2.
Brief facts of this case are that revisionist got married with respondent on 02.10.1998.
At that time, Sh. Avdhesh Kumar was unemployed, however, later on, he started working as Junior Scientist at D.U. in a contractual post.
Initially, they both stayed at Maujpur in the house of revisionist as jointly agreed by them.

However, Sh. Avdesh Kumar had assured the revisionist that they would shift to rented accommodation once he landed up job after completing her M.Sc., the revisionist landed up job as a Teacher in a Government School.
On 25.09.1999, Sh. Avdhesh Kumar has also landed up job as a Lecturer at Pant Nagar.
It is alleged that Sh. Avdhesh Kumar used to extract money from the revisionist on one pretext or the other.
On 05.12.1999, one daughter was born out of the wedlock.
After the birth of daughter, the revisionist requested many times to Sh. Avdhesh Kumar to take her to Pant Nagar but Sh. Avdhesh Kumar was not willing.
Sh. Avdhesh Kumar used to meet the petitioner on weekends.
3. On 11.04.2022, one son was born out of the wedlock.
Feeling aggrieved, the revisionist had purchased one Flat at Shalimar Garden, Ghaziabad, UP out of some contribution from parents, her own savings and remaining on installments.
The father-in-law, brother-in-law and sister-in-law also started residing there.

It is alleged that Sh. Avdhesh Kumar and his family members used to taunt her by saying "tu toh bhangan hai, hamare ghar kahi se aa gayi, hum toh iss ka haath ka paani bhi nahi piyenge, hamara toh dharam bharast ho jayega".

Thereafter, the petitioner has levelled several allegations primarily against the Sh. Avdhesh Kumar of subjecting her to cruelty-by entering into extramarital relation, and by giving physical torture.
On various occasions, Sh. Avdhesh Kumar used to beat the revisionist.
On the basis of statement of complainant, present FIR came to be registered.
After completion of necessary formalities, charge-sheet was filed in the concerned Court.
Vide order dated 18.11.2022, Ld. MM had framed charge only against Sh. Avdhesh Kumar for the offences punishable u/s 498A/ 406 of IPC.
However, the remaining respondents were discharged.

The said order is challenged primarily on the ground that as per the statement of complainant u/s 161 Cr.P.C.
dated 10.09.2011, there is clear averment that the father-in-law Narayan Singh, sister-in- law Madhu and Priyanka and brother-in-law Atul Kumar were brought by the husband of complainant to the LIG Flat at Shalimar Garden, Ghaziabad and on the instigation of all these accused persons,
the husband of the revisionist used to commit cruelties for bringing less dowry from her parents and in connivance of each other, she was thrown out of the said house by all of them after beating.
Thereafter, she came back to parental home.
4. This court has heard Ld. Counsel Sh. C. S. Tomar, for revisionist, Ld. Addl. PP for State for respondent no. 1 and Sh. V. K. Bhushan, Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 2 to 5
and have perused the record.

sentences.text: This court has perused the order dated 19-05-2022 of Ld. MM as well as the charge-sheet.
It is noted that no date, time and place has been mentioned in the original complaint of revisionist as to when she had been subjected to cruelty on the part of respondents herein.
Only vague and omnibus allegations have been levelled against the respondents.

6. In Preeti Gupta & Anr. Vs. State of Jharkhand, (2010) 7 SCC 3363, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India stated that, "the tendency of implicating husband and all his immediate relations is not uncommon.

entities.text: Preeti Gupta & Anr. Vs. State of Jharkhand, (2010) 7 SCC 3363
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At times, even after the conclusion of the criminal trial, it is difficult to ascertain the real truth.
Hence, the courts have to be extremely careful and cautious in dealing with these complaints and must take pragmatic realities into consideration while dealing with matrimonial cases."

7. In Anju Vs. Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors., Crl. Rev. P. 730/2016 decided on 04-02-2019, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi held that, "9. Revisional Court has in my view committed no error in coming to the conclusion that apart from general and omnibus allegations roping in all the relations,
there is no material on record to justify framing of charge under Section 498A/34 IPC.

entities.text: Anju Vs. Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Ors., Crl. Rev. P. 730/2016
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It may be noted that charge has already been framed against the husband and he is facing trial.
10. For a charge to be framed, the evidence gathered by the prosecution should not only give rise to suspicion but there should be grave suspicion that the accused have committed the offence.

11. In the present case apart from bald, omnibus allegations without their being any specifics about date time or place, there is no incriminating material found by the prosecution even during investigation to give rise to grave suspicion against the respondents."
8.

In Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors, Crl. Appeal no. 195/22, Arising out of SLP (Crl.) no. 6545/20 dated 08-02-2022, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that, "18.
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of Section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes, without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar & Ors, Crl. Appeal no. 195/22
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute,
if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."
9. In light of the above-stated findings and ruling of Superior courts, this court finds that there is no illegality or infirmity in the order dated 19-05-2022 and 18-11-2022 of the Ld. Trial Court.
Accordingly, the revision petition stands dismissed.

The trial court record be sent back to the Ld.
Trial Court with copy of this judgment and thereafter, revision file be segregated and consigned to Record Room.
ANNOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT
